rules.cwe_name: Data Processing Errors
rules.description: Legacy category for incorrect handling or transformation of structured data.

rules.cwe_name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor
rules.description: External links that open in a new tab or window but do not specify link type 'noopener' or 'noreferrer' are a potential security risk.

rules.cwe_name: Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior
rules.description: If the id of an HTML attribute is malformed, its interpretation may be browser-dependent.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
rules.description: Instantiating a template using a user-controlled object is vulnerable to local file read and potential remote code execution.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')
rules.description: Building a shell command string with values from the enclosing environment may cause subtle bugs or vulnerabilities.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Handling of Case Sensitivity
rules.description: Middleware with case-sensitive paths do not protect endpoints with case-insensitive paths.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of CRLF Sequences ('CRLF Injection')
rules.description: Untrusted CR or LF characters are not neutralized before use in line-delimited protocol metadata.

rules.cwe_name: Dead Code
rules.description: If a dollar assertion '$' appears in a regular expression before another term that cannot match the empty string, then this assertion can never match, so the entire regular expression cannot match any string.

rules.cwe_name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
rules.description: Downloading executables and other sensitive files over an insecure connection opens up for potential man-in-the-middle attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Document Type Definition
rules.description: Parsing user input as an XML document with external entity expansion is vulnerable to XXE attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Dead Code
rules.description: If a dollar assertion '$' appears in a regular expression before another term that cannot match the empty string, then this assertion can never match, so the entire regular expression cannot match any string.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Input Validation
rules.description: Prepending a backslash to an ordinary character in a string does not have any effect, and may make regular expressions constructed from this string behave unexpectedly.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Argument Delimiters in a Command ('Argument Injection')
rules.description: Building a shell command string with values from the enclosing environment may cause subtle bugs or vulnerabilities.

rules.cwe_name: Use of Externally-Controlled Format String
rules.description: Using external input in format strings can lead to garbled output.

rules.cwe_name: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
rules.description: Some mathematical operations on random numbers can cause bias in the results and compromise security.

rules.cwe_name: Reliance on Undefined, Unspecified, or Implementation-Defined Behavior
rules.description: If an HTML element has two attributes with the same name but different values, its behavior may be browser-dependent.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
rules.description: Using externally controlled strings to construct code may allow a malicious user to execute arbitrary code.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Control of Document Type Definition
rules.description: Parsing user input as an XML document with external entity expansion is vulnerable to XXE attacks.

rules.cwe_name: Inadequate Encryption Strength
rules.description: Using a weak cryptographic key can allow an attacker to compromise security.

rules.cwe_name: Improper Restriction of Recursive Entity References in DTDs ('XML Entity Expansion')
rules.description: Parsing user input as an XML document with arbitrary internal entity expansion is vulnerable to denial-of-service attacks.
